newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand chief defends baht decision.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand chief defends baht decision.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond on Friday defended the bank's decision to float the baht, saying it was made through established procedure with the knowledge of Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and the ministry's permanent secretary.
Rerngchai said in a statement that the decision was not exclusively his, saying it was an agreement reached by senior central bank and finance ministry officials responsible for such policy.
"The governor has never issued instructions or taken decisions contrary to proposals made by senior central bank officials. Any such accusations are therefore groundless," he said.
Rerngchai's statement was a response to some Thai media reports that Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh had directly ordered him to float the baht.

"Some reports said the prime minister ordered the central bank governor to change the exchange rate system. But under legal and established prodecure...which can be verified, it is the governor who would make such proposal to the finance minister for his approval before it is forwarded to the prime minister," he said.
The Bank of Thailand on July 2 let the baht loose on a new managed float regime which replaced an earlier practice of pegging the baht to a basket of currencies.
The baht has since declined by more than 20 percent and sparked criticism that the central bank switched to the new system without proper consideration.
Rerngchai's statement came amid rumours that the central bank governor may be under pressure to resign.
